what: Per-work count of [sic:]/[var:] markers standing on columns nobody has read at Migne’s plate, for every work marked englishState:"ours". The CEILING the ratchet enforces.
rule: plate-gate.mjs --ratchet fails if a work absent here carries ANY uncovered marker, or if a work listed here goes UP. Falls are fine and are a reason to re-freeze. Re-freeze ONLY after reading plates, never to make a red gate green.
refreeze_2026_09_05: ⚑ THE CEILING ROSE 889 -> 928 AND NO WORK GOT WORSE. On 2026-09-05 plate-gate.mjs was found to widen a read's range end by three bands unconditionally — right for a bare `0719`, wrong for a banded `0094D`, which is already at band D, so the +3 spilled into bands A-C OF THE NEXT COLUMN and silently licensed markers on pages nobody had read. Fixing it did not add a marker anywhere; it corrected the MEASUREMENT of a legacy backlog this session never touched. The 39 newly-visible markers belong to works shipped long before the gate existed (11613 +8, 8969 +5, 8959 +4, 8980 +3, 8992 +3, 8988 +1, 8968 +1, 8970 +2, and singles elsewhere). 8950 Liber Genesis, the work shipping in this session, added ZERO — 0 uncovered of 99 markers, every one on a column read at the plate. ⛔ This is NOT the case the no-re-freeze rule forbids. That rule exists so a REGRESSION is never tidied away, and re-freezing here records no claim about any plate: 928 is simply the true count under a working instrument, where 889 was the false one. Ruled by Wilson, 2026-09-05, on that distinction.
